featured_reviews.name: anil mahindrakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
As someone who is always on the hunt for great desserts, Pinka Bake House was such a pleasant surprise. Being a pure vegetarian bakery, I wasn’t sure what to expect, but their cheesecake and tiramisu completely won me over.

The cheesecake was incredibly creamy, rich, and perfectly balanced—not overly sweet, which is rare. Every bite felt fresh and indulgent. The tiramisu was equally impressive, with beautiful coffee notes and a light, velvety texture that kept me going back for more.

What I loved most was that these desserts didn’t feel like “good for a veg bakery”—they were genuinely outstanding on their own. If you’re a cheesecake or tiramisu lover and prefer pure vegetarian desserts, Pinka Bake House is absolutely worth trying.

Definitely one of my favorite dessert discoveries in Mumbai. 🍰✨

featured_reviews.name: Author Kailash amesur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pinka Cheese Cake Stall is a hidden gem that I stumbled upon during my recent outing. Their cheesecakes are a true delight for the taste buds. The range of flavors they offer is impressive, and each bite reveals a perfect balance of creaminess and sweetness.

What sets Pinka Cheese Cake apart is not just their delectable cakes but also the attention to detail in presentation. Each slice is a work of art that shows the passion and dedication that goes into crafting these desserts.

The stall itself has a charming and inviting ambiance, adding to the overall experience of indulging in their cheesecakes. The friendly staff enhances the visit, providing excellent customer service and making you feel right at home.

Whether you're a cheesecake enthusiast or simply looking to satisfy your sweet cravings, Pinka Cheese Cake Stall is a must-visit. I highly recommend trying their various flavors to experience a delightful symphony of taste in every bite. This place has definitely earned a spot on my list of favorites, and I can't wait to go back for more.

featured_reviews.name: Mehvish Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yesterday I visited Pinka Bake House, a delightful home bakery located in Powai, Mumbai. Known as Mumbai's first cheesecake stall.

Upon my friends' enthusiastic recommendations about their cheesecakes, we decided to sample a variety: Nutella Cheesecake, Lotus Biscoff Cheesecake, Blueberry Cheesecake, and a Black Forest Mousse. The Nutella and Lotus Biscoff cheesecakes were rich and delectable, but the Blueberry Cheesecake truly stood out—it was exceptional! I'd rate the Blueberry a stellar 100/10, the Nutella an 8.5/10, the Lotus a 9/10, and the creamy Black Forest Mousse a solid 8/10.

The portions were generous, and we couldn't finish everything. The kind lady serving us graciously packed the remaining cheesecakes for us to enjoy at home. The Blueberry Cheesecake has certainly won my heart. I'm looking forward to returning for more!

The ambiance is cozy with beautifully displayed desserts that instantly catch your eye and make the place feel warm and inviting.

Food Ratings:
•Sebastian Cake – 5/5
•French Vanilla Bombolini – 5/5
•Cookies – 4/5
•Pastries & Cakes – 4/5
•Chicken nuggets - 4/5
•Veg Russian Sandwich - 4/5

The bakery section shines far brighter than the savoury menu.

featured_reviews.name: Bilal Tajak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today, we went to Deliure around 8:00 PM and placed our order. The staff told us it would take 40–45 minutes. Despite the long delay, we waited patiently as we are regular customers. While we were sitting inside, a major parking issue was unfolding outside. It was entirely Deliure’s fault because they failed to arrange proper parking management, which caused a lot of trouble for the locals and led to a massive traffic jam. Consequently, people complained to the police. The local police and traffic police arrived at the scene and took two of Deliure's managers to the police station.
When we finally walked outside, we found that our vehicle had been fined. This happened even though we had parked our vehicle exactly where the Deliure staff had instructed us to. When we went back inside to confront the Deliure management about this, they bluntly told us that they were not responsible for the fine, and their behaviour towards us was extremely rude.
They could have easily informed us about the ongoing parking issue with the police while we were waiting inside for our order, and they could have asked us to move our vehicle. However, they chose not to do so, and because of their negligence, we ended up with a fine. Do we really deserve this treatment? We waited so long for our food, and in return, we had to pay a fine! Is this how they respect their regular customers?
Furthermore, this entire parking chaos and heavy order load escalated because Deliure was prioritizing online orders over offline walk-in customers. Their mentality is crystal clear—they only care about making money from online orders, making offline customers wait indefinitely, and leaving them in deep trouble when their vehicles get fined due to the establishment's mismanagement.

featured_reviews.name: Roshan Shanbhag
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sassy spoon is one of of our tried & tested spots for good food & great atmosphere! Service is on point & the service team is extremely efficient! We booked a table for 6 on Sunday the 31st Aug as we wanted to host our niece & nephews visiting from Bangalore and we confidently booked this place! Naturally you are looking forward to a great time with kids & be able to banter! However we realised upon reaching that its a live music sunday! All our chatting & bantering plans fell flat! While the live music artist was just about fine in his skills, the issue was around the loudness of the sound and the acoustics of the restaurant being unfavourable to handle that level of decibel made it an absolute noise fest! We were disappointed! We could hardly hear each other! I am unsure on how they can improve this but i find it unlikely of them doing it! So we have decided to avoid Sunday brunch/lunch from hereon as its not the atmosphere we prefer!

Ps: i am originally a Bangalorean and live music scene is extensive there but well managed with restaurants acoustic set ups and the sound levels are perfect with no interference if customers are willing to hear each other! May be you can consult some sound design experts!
